easy.def: Feeling upset because someone has something you want.
examples: I felt jealous of her new bike.
The cat is jealous of the new kitten.
Do not be jealous. You will get a turn.

more.def: Unhappy because you want what another person has.
examples: He felt jealous when his friend won the prize.
She was jealous of her brother's later bedtime.
The dog gets jealous when I pet the cat.
He felt jealousy.
Jealousy is a bad feeling.
Her jealousy grew.

more.def: A feeling of unhappiness because someone has something you want.
examples: He felt jealousy when his friend got a new bike.
Jealousy made her say a mean thing.
Her jealousy faded when she got her own turn.
I wear jeans.
The jeans are blue.
My jeans have pockets.

more.def: Strong pants that are usually made of blue cotton cloth called denim.
examples: I wear jeans to school.
My jeans have a hole in the knee.
She rolled up the cuffs of her jeans.

easy.def: A small, strong car for rough roads.
examples: We rode in a jeep.
The jeep drove up the hill.
The jeep has big wheels.

more.def: A small, sturdy vehicle that can drive on rough ground.
examples: The ranger drove a jeep over the bumpy trail.
We rode in an open jeep through the park.
The jeep splashed through the muddy stream.

easy.def: A soft, sweet food made from fruit juice.
examples: I like jelly on my toast.
The jelly is grape.
She spread jelly on bread.

more.def: A soft, sweet spread made from fruit juice and sugar.
examples: I put grape jelly on my sandwich.
She spread jelly on warm toast.
Grandma made strawberry jelly.

easy.def: Danger of being harmed or lost.
examples: The animals were in jeopardy.
Our trip is in jeopardy.
The game was in jeopardy.

more.def: A state of danger or risk of harm or loss.
examples: The animals were in jeopardy when the forest burned.
Our trip is in jeopardy because of the storm.
The game was in jeopardy because of the rain.
The bus made jerky stops.
A jerky ride.
The puppet moved in a jerky way.

more.def: Moving with sudden, short jumps and stops, rather than smoothly.
examples: The old bus made jerky stops all along the road.
The puppet moved in a funny, jerky way.
The video was jerky because the internet was slow.
I ate beef jerky.
The jerky was salty.
He packed jerky for the hike.

more.def: Meat that has been cut into strips and dried so that it is chewy and lasts a long time.
examples: The hikers packed beef jerky for a snack on the trail.
Jerky is salty and chewy and does not need a refrigerator.
Dad cut the meat into strips to make jerky.
It was just a jest.
He said it in jest.
The king liked a good jest.

more.def: A joke or something said to make people laugh.
examples: He said it in jest, so no one was upset.
The court jester told a jest that made the king laugh.
It was just a jest and not meant to be taken seriously.

easy.def: To say something to be funny.
examples: He likes to jest.
I was only jesting.
She jested with her friend.

more.def: To joke or say funny things.
examples: He likes to jest with his friends at lunch.
I was only jesting when I said the dog ate my homework.
She jested about her messy room and made us laugh.

easy.def: A funny person who joked for a king long ago.
examples: The jester made the king laugh.
A jester wore a funny hat.
The jester did a trick.

more.def: A person in the Middle Ages whose job was to tell jokes and do tricks to entertain a king or queen.
examples: The jester juggled three balls and told jokes to the king.
A jester wore a colorful hat with bells on it.
The jester's silly songs made the whole court laugh.
The jet flew over the town.
We rode on a jet.
A jet is fast.

more.def: A fast airplane with engines that push out hot air.
examples: The jet flew high above the clouds.
We flew on a jet to see my aunt.
A jet leaves a white trail across the sky.

easy.def: A strong stream of water or air.
examples: A jet of water shot up.
The fountain has a jet.
A jet of air blew the leaves.

more.def: A strong, thin stream of water, air or gas that comes out of a small hole.
examples: A jet of water shot up from the fountain.
The hose sent a jet across the yard.
A jet of steam came from the kettle.

easy.def: A beautiful stone that is worth a lot.
examples: The crown has a jewel.
The jewel sparkles.
She wore a jewel.

more.def: A valuable, shiny stone that has been cut and polished.
examples: The crown was covered with jewels.
A red jewel sparkled on the ring.
The pirate hid a chest of jewels.

easy.def: Rings, necklaces and bracelets that people wear.
examples: She wears jewelry.
The jewelry is shiny.
Mom keeps her jewelry in a box.

more.def: Things such as rings and necklaces that people wear to look nice.
examples: She put on her jewelry before the party.
The shop sells gold and silver jewelry.
The jewelry box was full of old necklaces.
